Definition: filth, i.e. (figuratively and specifically) an idolatrous object
BiblicalUsage: Some things God calls filth outright: the unclean creatures of the law, the idols in the high places, and the abominable practices Isaiah and Ezekiel saw in the temple courts. The word is not polite, and it is not meant to be — it names what revolts a holy God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Bible's bluntness here is mercy, because it will not let me call an idol a preference. If God calls it filth, I should call it filth too, and keep it out of my house and my heart.
